A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same FIRE/DDfire study. Their complete main text, equations, tables, figures, and appendices support reliable comparison; retained content can be matched across relocation and renumbering.

before.justification: v2 reports original image-reconstruction and phase-retrieval experiments, component ablations, runtime measurements, and supplementary analyses.

after.justification: v3 retains these empirical studies and adds ImageNet phase retrieval, DDS comparison results, and hyperparameter-sensitivity experiments.

M1.justification: Appendix H.5 and Algorithm 7 add an optional guided DDfire variant, used with HIO estimates for ImageNet OSF. It randomizes the guidance, combines it with the diffusion state, and adjusts FIRE's input variance and iteration allocation. The underlying FIRE algorithms and standard DDfire remain unchanged.

E1.justification: Table 4 extends OSF and CDP phase retrieval from FFHQ faces to ImageNet natural images. ImageNet was previously evaluated only on the linear reconstruction tasks. The original datasets, four linear tasks, and FFHQ phase-retrieval scenarios remain represented.

E2.justification: DDS, previously discussed but not evaluated, gains comparison rows across the linear tasks in Tables 2–3. Existing comparators remain. SNORE receives an algorithmic discussion without reported benchmark results, and the runtime plot and phase-retrieval comparator sets are unchanged.

E3.justification: Appendix H.4 and Table 6 revise DDfire's CDP budget from 800 to 100 NFEs and K from 80 to 10; OSF retains 800 NFEs. The new ImageNet OSF experiment uses HIO guidance. Appendix I adds a separate 50-image parameter-sweep design, while the existing 100-image validation protocol remains. Section 4 retains the general 800-NFE phase-retrieval description.

E4.justification: New Appendix I and Figures 7–10 systematically examine sensitivity to K and delta through PSNR and LPIPS across all four linear tasks. This substantially extends the analysis beyond v2's component ablation. The original ablation, variance-tracking analyses, and reconstruction examples are retained.

E5.justification: Figures 7–10 introduce error bars on the tuning curves, but neither their statistical meaning nor their calculation is specified. The four-run OSF selection procedure and single-run CDP protocol are unchanged; no additional seed information or significance testing is reported.

E6.justification: Tables 2–4 add DDS and ImageNet phase-retrieval results; DDfire reports ImageNet PSNRs of 29.93 for guided OSF and 28.91 for CDP. FFHQ CDP PSNR/LPIPS/FID changes from 30.01/0.1232/23.49 to 30.16/0.1186/23.30 alongside revised settings, so this is not an established same-setting improvement. Figures 7–10 add tuning outcomes. Existing linear-method scores and FFHQ OSF scores remain unchanged.

T1.justification: Appendix H.5 adds Gaussian modeling assumptions and a derivation of the guided estimate, effective variance, and sufficient-statistic interpretation in Equations 82–87. Theorem 1, its proof, and the existing VP/VE and convergence derivations remain unchanged.

C1.justification: The conclusion broadens the phase-retrieval performance claim from FFHQ to FFHQ and ImageNet and includes DDS among the linear comparators outperformed. The abstract's scientific claims and the five stated main contributions otherwise retain their scope.

C2.justification: Appendix I newly acknowledges sensitivity to hyperparameter selection, particularly for localized degradation such as inpainting. Appendix H.5 explains the guidance tradeoff: greater added noise supports the Gaussian approximation but weakens the guidance's influence.

D1.justification: The abstract adds an implementation repository address, although Appendix H.4 retains the release-on-acceptance wording. New details include DDS's 100 NFEs, 50 CG iterations, eta of 0.8, and grid-search tuning, plus the guidance-noise prescription and its 50-times-error-variance setting for ImageNet OSF.

R1.justification: Sections 2–3 and new Appendix G substantially expand positioning relative to PnP and Langevin methods, including detailed DDS, DiffPIR, and SNORE comparisons with pseudocode. New citations include Renaud et al., Laumont et al., Jalal et al., and Bouman and Buzzard. The RePaint citation and the RePaint/DDNM+ time-travel discussion are removed.

P1.justification: Localized rewrites clarify the HQS connection, variance estimation, and relationships to other methods. New appendix sections are inserted, with implementation details and supplementary results renumbered. The main section sequence and most existing exposition remain unchanged.

P2.justification: v3 adds four paired tuning figures and Algorithms 4–7, and expands Table 4 from two FFHQ operator groups to four dataset/operator groups. Tables 2–3 gain DDS rows, and several displays move. The original figure images are retained, including those renumbered as Figures 11–15.

improvement.justification: v3 strengthens evidence for phase retrieval beyond faces and improves understanding of method differences and tuning limitations through ImageNet experiments, DDS comparisons, and the new appendix analyses. These provide a useful overall gain in coverage and transparency. Undefined tuning-plot error bars and the retained general 800-NFE description limit reporting clarity.
